message.content: {"caption":"Two-panel categorical point chart comparing Memory Quality scores across memory methods for two language-model backbones.","description":"The chart has two vertically stacked panels. Both use Memory Quality (MQ) on the y-axis and the categories LangMem, A-Mem, Mem0, Mem0ᵍ, AgeMem-noRL, and AgeMem on the x-axis. Blue circles denote Baselines, a red star denotes AgeMem, and a gray dashed horizontal line with a pale gray band denotes Avg. Baseline. Thin vertical stems connect the scores to the average-baseline line; the AgeMem score is additionally outlined by a red box. In the upper panel, labeled “(a) Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct,” the y-axis runs from 0.3 to 0.6. Printed scores are LangMem 0.498, A-Mem 0.512, Mem0 0.527, Mem0ᵍ 0.460, AgeMem-noRL 0.364, and AgeMem 0.533. The baseline scores rise through Mem0, then fall at Mem0ᵍ and fall further at AgeMem-noRL; AgeMem is the highest score. The dashed average-baseline line is approximately 0.472. In the lower panel, labeled “(b) Qwen3-4B-Instruct,” the y-axis runs from 0.4 to 0.7. Printed scores are LangMem 0.465, A-Mem 0.587, Mem0 0.543, Mem0ᵍ 0.534, AgeMem-noRL 0.430, and AgeMem 0.605. A-Mem is the highest baseline; scores then decline through Mem0 and Mem0ᵍ, with a further drop at AgeMem-noRL. AgeMem is the highest score overall in this panel.
